label: Weak, sparse: first copy-phase input of length-3 sequences starting with h/q/u (plus scattered other contexts)
explanation: Very sparse (0.018% of steps), low-magnitude feature (max 0.256). The strongest activations are at step L+1 of length-3 sequences, where the first original token is fed back as input, when that token is h, q or u (top example: h w c <DEL> [h] w). The highest ones also have c as the last original token. Even there precision is only about 0.19: most h/q/u length-3 sequences do not fire it. The other ~75% of activation mass is spread across unrelated contexts: original-phase step 2 after a leading c (c c [x]), the last copy steps of long sequences, and step L+1 of length-4 sequences. Each of these has precision of about 1% or lower. Tried: recall_idx==1 & L<=4 (F1 0.01), prev2==c in the original phase (F1 0.007), and a two-clause disjunction (mass recall 0.53 but precision 0.02). It never fires at t=0/1 or on incorrect-copy steps. No coherent description reaches useful precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=4: h, u, q, d; t=5: h, q, 3, u; t=17: h, 3, q, b) and the next token to output (most: c, w, k, 2, d, e; least: r, g, p, i); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, L=3 & t=4, t=3.
